summary: Tested WhatsApp OTP auth (simulation mode) end-to-end. 13/13 backend pytest cases pass and all requested frontend flows (signup->onboarding, login->dashboard, admin email login->/admin, cross-links, resend cooldown UI) pass. Uncovered one CRITICAL migration bug in production DB: the legacy `email_1` sparse-unique index co-existed with the new `email_partial_unique` index, causing HTTP 500 on the second creator/brand signup (DuplicateKeyError on email=null). Testing agent manually dropped the stale index to unblock; the startup code path in server.py that is supposed to migrate it never fires (create_index of the differently-named partial index succeeds without raising OperationFailure, so the fallback drop is skipped).

critical.issue: DuplicateKeyError on users.email=null caused HTTP 500 for any 2nd+ OTP signup because startup migration in server.py (~lines 2071-2088) does not drop the legacy `email_1` sparse-unique index. `_ensure_partial_unique` only drops the old index inside its OperationFailure fallback, but creating an index with a NEW name (`email_partial_unique`) succeeds silently, so the stale `email_1` (unique+sparse) is left behind. Mongo sparse indexes still enforce uniqueness across explicit null values -> duplicate. Testing agent manually ran `db.users.drop_index('email_1')` to unblock. Recommend: unconditionally drop any pre-existing single-field indexes on `email` and `phone` (except `_id_`) before creating the partial-unique replacement. Same latent risk exists for `phone` if it ever had a plain unique index.

action_items: Harden startup index migration in server.py (_ensure_partial_unique or a new one-time migration): always drop any existing single-field non-_id index on `users.email` and `users.phone` before creating the partial-unique variant. Alternatively, delete the field entirely when null (store phone-only accounts without an `email` key) so partial index skips them and any lingering sparse-unique wouldn't match either.
critical_code_review_comments: OTP verify endpoint stores `signup_role` on user even for `login` path — that branch is fine, but on signup you never validate that `payload.role` matches `record.role` from the initial request; a client could request as creator then verify as brand. Consider trusting the DB-recorded role only.
`_send_aisensy_otp` logs the raw OTP to backend.err.log even in simulation mode. This is expected in dev but explicitly document/gate behind ENV=='dev' to prevent accidental prod exposure.
server.py is ~2400 lines — split into routers (auth, creator, brand, admin, campaigns, payments) for maintainability.

`display_name = (payload.name or existing_user.get('name') if existing_user else payload.name) or 'User'` has confusing operator precedence — behaves as `(payload.name or existing_user.get('name')) if existing_user else payload.name`. Works but worth an explicit ternary.

context_for_next_testing_agent: The failing signups were due to a stale `email_1` sparse-unique Mongo index that was NOT removed by the startup migration in server.py. Testing agent dropped it manually. If a fresh DB is used or the index is reintroduced, subsequent creator/brand signups will 500 with DuplicateKeyError on `email: null`. Confirm main agent has patched _ensure_partial_unique (or added an explicit migration) to always remove legacy single-field indexes before creating the partial variant. All other flows (30s cooldown, 5-wrong-code lockout, 409 duplicate signup, 404 unknown-login-phone, admin email login, invalid phone, resend cooldown UI, cross-links, /onboarding/creator + /dashboard redirects) are working correctly.
rca of the issue: Backend 500 on 2nd signup — root cause: `_ensure_partial_unique` in server.py creates `email_partial_unique` under a NEW name. Because the name differs, MongoDB accepts creating it alongside the legacy `email_1` (unique, sparse) without raising OperationFailure, so the fallback that drops legacy single-field indexes never runs. Sparse unique still forbids more than one document with `email: null` (sparse only excludes docs missing the field, not docs with an explicit null). Fix: unconditionally scan and drop any single-field index on `email`/`phone` (except `_id_`) whose options differ from the target partial-unique spec, then create the new one. Mitigation applied by testing agent: `db.users.drop_index('email_1')`.
